texts.preamble: A.Subramanian vs The Commissioner Of Police on 21 March, 2025 Before The Madurai Bench Of Madras High Court Dated: 21.03.2025 Coram : The Hon'Ble Mr.Justice P.Dhanabal W.P(MD)No.7658 of 2025 A.Subramanian . Vs 1.The Commissioner of Police, Trichy City, Trichy. 2.The Inspector of Police, Airport Police Station, Trichy. . Prayer: Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution o India, praying this Court to issue a Writ of Mandamus directing the respondents not to interfere in the business of the petitioner tea namely Sri Naganathar Tea Stall at No.1/1, 1/2, Pattathammal Street Pudukottai main road, Airport, Trichy, during night hours and consi his representation dated 15.02.2025 in the light of G.O.Ms.No.61 La welfare and skill development (K2) dated 02.06.2022. For Petitioner : Mr.N.Ananda Kumar For Respondents : Mr.R.M.Anbunithi Additional Public Prosecutor 1/5 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 02/04/2025 04:34:56 pm ) Order
texts.facts: to the petitioner he is running a tea stall in the name and style of Sri Naganathar Tea Stall at No.1/1, 1/2, Pattathammal Street, Pudukottai main road, Airport, Trichy. He got license from Trichy Municipality and the same was duly renewed. He has also got license from the Food & Safety Department to sell the food products. While so, the second respondent insisted the petitioner not to open the Tea Stall beyond 11.00 p.m. As per G.O.Ms.No.61 Labour Welfare and Skill Development (K2), dated 02.06.2022, he is entitled to run the Tea Stall 24 hours. However, the second respondent threatened the petitioner not to run the shop beyond 11.00 p.m. In this regard, he has given a representation on 15.02.2025, but the same was not considered. Hence, this petition has been filed. Therefore, the second respondent advised the petitioner not to park the vehicles in the road and they have not insisted the petitioner to close the shop beyond 11.00 p.m.
texts.arguments: 3.The learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent police would submit that the petitioner's Tea Stall located in the main area and the customers used to park vehicles in the road, thereby, causing hindrance to the general public.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 3.The learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent police would submit that the petitioner's Tea Stall located in the main area and the customers used to park vehicles in the road, thereby, causing hindrance to the general public.
